summary: Order quote timeouts originate in pricing-engine, not in the market-data-service deploy the report points to. At 12:04:00Z config change cfg-3120 ramped the feature flag flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100, moving all quote traffic onto the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (paths=20000, 3-9s per computation). Because request_rate stayed flat (~640 req/s), CPU went from ~40% to 99-100% and each quote blew its 2000ms internal budget, producing "request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget)" errors; order-service's 2500ms client timeout then fired. market-data-service (deploy dep-6111 at 11:56) is healthy throughout (p99 ~40ms, CPU ~45%, error_rate ~0.2%), ruling out the reported suspect. Fault category: config_change (feature-flag ramp).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Feature-flag ramp of GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator saturated pricing-engine CPU, causing quote deadline breaches
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 (12:04Z) ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 on pricing-engine. The GreeksV2 calculator runs a 20000-path Monte-Carlo costing 3-9s of CPU per quote, ~100x the previous path. With request_rate unchanged (~640 req/s), running it for all traffic saturated CPU to 100%, so each quote exceeded its 2000ms budget ('request deadline exceeded'), and order-service's 2500ms client timeout fired, failing orders at the quote step.

causal_chain.claim: All quote traffic now uses the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo (20000 paths, 3-9s)
pricing-engine CPU saturates to 99-100% despite flat request_rate
Quotes breach the 2000ms internal budget -> deadline exceeded errors
order-service 2500ms client timeout fires; orders fail at quote step

assumptions: The greeks_v2 flag directly gates which calculator handles a quote (supported by the metric onset coinciding with the flag ramp).
The 12:05 metric bucket boundary is consistent with a 12:04 change taking effect within seconds.

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy caused quote latency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-6111 (market-data-service v5.2.0, protobuf quote serialization, 11:56Z) degraded the quote path, propagating to pricing-engine and order-service timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service is healthy throughout (p99 ~40ms, CPU ~45%, error_rate ~0.2%, no logs at onset). The slow component is pricing-engine's local GreeksV2Calculator, not the market-data call. The deploy precedes onset by 10 minutes with no matching step change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation from market-open volume (recurrence of HIST-113)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Traffic growth exceeded provisioned pricing-engine capacity, saturating CPU and causing quote timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate is flat (~640 req/s) across onset; there is no load increase. CPU rose with identical traffic, which points to a per-request cost increase (the flag ramp), not demand.

facts.statement: order-service quote-timeout ERRORs begin 12:06:10Z, matching a pricing-engine degradation.
The only change in the window is config cfg-3120 ramping greeks_v2 rollout 5 -> 100 at 12:04:00Z.
pricing-engine's GreeksV2 calculator executes 20000-path Monte-Carlos taking 3-9s per symbol.
pricing-engine CPU went ~40% -> 99-100% and p99 ~60ms -> ~2600ms exactly at the 12:05 bucket.
pricing-engine request_rate is flat across onset, ruling out a load-driven cause.
market-data-service stayed healthy (p99 ~40ms, CPU ~45%, error_rate ~0.2%) with only a TLS-cipher WARN, ruling out dep-6111 as the cause.

assumptions: The greeks_v2 feature flag selects which quote calculator executes, so a 5->100 ramp moved essentially all traffic onto GreeksV2.
The 12:04 flag change becomes effective within the 12:05 metric bucket (sub-minute propagation).
Order-service's 2500ms timeout is the client side of pricing-engine's 2000ms internal quote budget.
(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) pricing-engine error_rate rose to ~11-12% and order-service error_rate to ~8% at onset.

timeline.event: market-data-service logs a single benign 'deprecated TLS cipher' WARN (last notable event before onset)
deploy dep-6111 to market-data-service v5.2.0 (protobuf serialization) — reported suspect
pricing-engine CPU jumps to 99-100%, p99 to ~2600ms, error_rate to ~11%; order-service error_rate to ~8%
pricing-engine begins logging slow GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo computations (6-8s)
order-service begins logging 2500ms pricing-engine quote timeouts
pricing-engine logs 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget)'

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back cfg-3120: set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or 0).
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the trigger; reverting the flag should restore pricing-engine CPU/latency and clear the quote timeouts without touching market-data-service.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back dep-6111 (market-data-service); it is not implicated.
recommended_actions.rationale: market-data-service is healthy; a rollback would add risk without addressing the fault.

recommended_actions.action: Before re-ramping greeks_v2, benchmark its CPU cost and gate the rollout on headroom.
recommended_actions.rationale: GreeksV2 costs ~100x CPU per quote; a 100% rollout saturates capacity at normal traffic.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-calculator CPU/latency metrics and an alert on quote-budget breaches, plus progressive-rollout canary guardrails for flags touching hot paths.
recommended_actions.rationale: Detect expensive-calculator regressions and stop flag ramps automatically before they saturate CPU.

data_gaps: No metric series for pricing-engine restarts was inspected; restart-related effects not fully excluded (CPU saturation pattern makes restarts unlikely to be causal).
No direct measurement of GreeksV1 vs GreeksV2 per-request CPU cost; the ~100x figure is inferred from log timings (3-9s Monte-Carlo) and CPU jump at flat request rate.
Config-audit shard 2/3 was initially unreachable; after retry only cfg-3120 appeared, so no other config changes are expected but a shard outage could in principle have hidden changes.

findings.statement: Dependency graph: order-service calls pricing-engine (http); pricing-engine calls market-data-service (http) and redis-cache. Edge direction is caller -> callee.
The first config-audit query returned partial:true (shard 2/3 missing); a retry returned the complete single change cfg-3120, so no other config changes exist in the window.

The onset aligns with cfg-3120 (12:04) plus ~1-2 min propagation, not with dep-6111 (11:56, 10 min earlier): all pricing-engine/order-service metrics change exactly at the 12:05 bucket while market-data-service (the deploy target) is unaffected.
